expectations.text: The ADR states context, decision, alternatives, and consequences distinctly
expectations.evidence: Write tool created docs/decisions/ADR-001-event-sourcing-for-orders-service.md with separate headed sections: '## Context' (mutable rows, auditor/support requirements, constraints), '## Decision' (adopt event sourcing, stream as system of record, projections for reporting), '## Alternatives Considered', and '## Consequences' (6 bullets). Also includes Status and Date headers.

expectations.text: Trade-offs and rejected options are recorded, not just the winning choice
expectations.evidence: '## Alternatives Considered' contains all three options from decision-context.md, each with Pros/Cons and a verdict line: audit table ('Rejected: Gives an approximation of history rather than an authoritative one'), CDC ('Rejected: ... CDC output is not a durable contract across schema evolution'), and event sourcing ('Accepted: ...'). Cons of the winning option are recorded too (projection rebuilds, event versioning, eventual consistency, operational complexity), and Consequences names the reporting service's tolerance of replication lag.

expectations.text: The document is written in timeless language describing current state
expectations.evidence: Text uses present/declarative tense throughout: 'The orders service stores mutable order rows and emits best-effort webhooks.', 'Adopt event sourcing for orders. Order state transitions are persisted as an append-only event stream', 'The event stream becomes the system of record', 'Read models are projections and are eventually consistent.' No meeting-minutes narration ('we discussed', 'last Tuesday', 'will decide later'); only minor time-flavored phrase is 'are now ongoing obligations', which still describes the current state.
